title: Recording in every idiom: Sons of the Pioneers, Gunsmoke and Hawaii Five-O
summary: He says he has recorded everything from symphonies to the Sons of the Pioneers and background music for television shows with no credit.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Mmm-hmm, she sure is. You've been heard on a lot of recordings that aren't Jazz recordings around this town, because you do a lot of recording work in all idioms, right?
Yeah. I would say all idioms from symphony to Sons of the Pioneers -- I recorded with them many years ago. So I've run the gamut.
How far back does that go, with Sons of the Pioneers?
Sons of the Pioneers? That was in the Fifties. That was when...
...what was the guy's name? He was Festus on the show, on Gunsmoke... Ken Perry(?) or something?
I'm sorry. I don't know that show.

He played Matt Dillon's sidekick, or Jim Arnett's sidekick on Gunsmoke. After... I can't think of his name either. Do you know the first sidekick he had on Gunsmoke? That was probably before your time, too.
Well, I'm afraid that wasn't a show I watched often.
Well, I watched it because that's one of the shows I used to record music, background music on -- Gunsmoke and Hawaii Five-O and all those shows. Those were

the shows you just work; you get no credit, but you just do the work. One of my main beefs is that all of the hundreds of shows I've done, starting with Life of Riley, which happened to be on film, we get no residuals.
